title: [Kernel] reloading fused_moe config on the last chunk (#6210)
gain_evidence: In our experiments, this can yield a ~5% speedup on average (see plot for a general idea of the diff in performance).

experiments.name: fused_experts_last_chunk_config_reload
experiments.workload: Author ran fused_moe chunked execution (follow-up to the #6029 chunking mechanism) and observed that reloading the Triton kernel config sized for the smaller last chunk yields a ~5% average speedup across their experiments (reported as a performance plot, no tabulated numbers).
experiments.note: Diff refactors the config lookup in fused_experts into a try_get_optimal_moe_config helper wrapped in functools.partial, then calls get_config_func(tokens_in_chunk) to RELOAD the config for the final (smaller) chunk instead of reusing the full CHUNK_SIZE config. Number source: PR body 'this can yield a ~5% speedup on average'; only a plot is attached, no absolute before/after values.

reported.scope: end-to-end fused_moe layer throughput averaged across the author's unspecified MoE model/batch experiments, shown only as a performance plot
reported.scale_short: Author gives a ~5% average from a plot over whole-layer fused_moe runs on GPU; our isolated microbench cannot reproduce the Triton-kernel autotune path on CPU. TO MAKE 1:1: run fused_experts on a CUDA box with a real MoE weight set and a batch whose final chunk is smaller than VLLM_FUSED_MOE_CHUNK_SIZE, comparing per-call latency with and without the last-chunk config reload.
reported.scale_note: The win is a GPU Triton autotune effect: the last chunk is smaller than CHUNK_SIZE, so reusing the full-chunk kernel config is suboptimal; reloading a config tuned for the smaller chunk recovers ~5%. No absolute baseline published (plot only), and the path only exercises on GPU, so direction is genuine but magnitude is not CPU-reproducible.
